answer: Quadratic staking erosion forces each validator to lock collateral proportional to the square of its stake, making a Sybil cluster of n identities require O(n²) capital. The umber coefficient calibrates the slashing curve so that marginal penalty grows as stake², while the beacon checkpoint timestamps each epoch to prevent replay. An island of honest validators therefore experiences attack cost exceeding any extractable value V by a factor of Ω(n).
